A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work on data geometry and generalization below the edge of stability. All 54 pages of v1 and 49 pages of v2, including Appendices A–J, are readable. Text, equations and figures can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original synthetic regression and MNIST-versus-Gaussian experiments, including learning curves, neuron activation statistics and depth-dependent prediction errors.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain original experimental outcomes and report revised radial-concentration results. The retained experiments qualify as original results of this work.

M1.justification: The two-layer ReLU model, squared loss, gradient-descent procedure and stable-interpolation construction remain the same. The depth index and gradient-dynamics discussion analyze the existing model rather than introduce a new training or inference component.

E1.justification: The learning tasks and MNIST, Gaussian, sphere and line-mixture coverage remain. The radial experiment shifts from α = {1, 5, 10, 50} to {0.1, 0.3, 1.5, 5.0}, changing the represented input distributions toward stronger boundary concentration within the same family.

E2.justification: No comparison algorithm is added or removed from the experiments. The comparisons continue to apply the same network and training procedure to different input geometries. Changed theoretical comparisons and citations do not establish evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The radial sweep uses a revised concentration grid, and v2 introduces depth-quantile curves and area summaries as geometric diagnostics. Existing sample-size scaling procedures, OLS fitting, clean-MSE evaluation, training budgets and shared-initialization controls are retained.

E4.justification: New Figures 1(a) and 2(b–c) examine how depth profiles vary with radial concentration, ambient dimension for line mixtures, and dimension for uniform balls. The radial sensitivity study is revised, while the existing activation, Hessian and MNIST depth-error analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions average the Section 4.1 experiments over six random seeds and retain the same OLS regression summaries, including slope dispersion and fit statistics. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing practice is introduced.

E6.justification: The radial plot reports replacement slopes for the revised α grid; even the shared α = 5 setting changes from −0.292 to −0.174. These changes do not establish an overall performance improvement. New depth-area values are reported, and the main MNIST plot drops its −0.013 correlation annotation. The intrinsic-dimension plot and Appendix C results are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds the depth-quantile function and concentration index, generic depth-decomposition equations, and mixture-depth reasoning. Remark 3.7 adds a hidden-bias-free spherical-rate statement. Appendices D, E and F revise mathematical arguments, and Appendix I corrects hidden-bias derivative signs. The principal isotropic, mixture and flat-interpolation theorem rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract's central claims about intrinsic-dimensional adaptation, radial concentration and stable memorization are retained. v2 makes the quantitative depth framework an explicit contribution and describes mixture-component dependence as at most polynomial rather than at most linear, without changing the displayed main bound.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a substantive weak-gradient trapping explanation and discusses possible relevance beyond ReLU. Sections 3.2–3.3 and 5 qualify the concentration index for anisotropic data and explain bound looseness through the rectangle-versus-area interpretation. The pre-existing two-layer/deep-network limitation is retained and expanded.

D1.justification: Appendix C preserves the network widths, learning rates, clipping thresholds, teacher/noise setup, MNIST normalization and Hessian-estimation procedure. No new implementation instructions, hardware information or code/data access disclosure is supplied; the revised concentration grid is an experimental-setting change.

R1.justification: v2 adds nonparametric-estimation discussion and references such as Schmidt-Hieber (2020) and DeVore et al. (2025), and frames its novelty more explicitly as a depth-based extension of Liang et al. (2025). The Wen et al. (2023) comparison is removed, while an already-cited Wu and Su (2023) result receives a new bias-free-model connection.

P1.justification: The contribution narrative and Section 3 are substantially reorganized around depth and shatterability, with isotropic results preceding low-dimensional adaptation. The depth discussion formerly in Section 4.3 is moved and expanded. v2 also adds Appendix B.2, a dedicated limitations paragraph and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts conference formatting, combines the title, abstract and introduction on the opening page, and moves the contents to the supplement. The original geometry triptych is redistributed across two expanded figures with new depth plots. Experimental panels are reordered and the main MNIST scatterplot is redrawn; most existing plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit depth proxy, supporting visualizations, reorganized explanation and anisotropic-data qualifications make the central argument easier to assess; Appendix I also corrects derivative signs. These benefits support a limited improvement, partly offset by precision problems: the introduction calls the bounds matching despite Remark 3.9 acknowledging non-tightness, and the revised projection identity in Appendix F.1 omits a normalization factor. The principal guarantees and most experimental evidence remain unchanged.
